title: Pointwise completeness is invariant under restriction of scalars
statement: Let C be a small site with topology J, R and B sheaves of commutative rings and φ:R→B a morphism. Choose unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of their module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on C and on every slice. Let M∈D(B), U∈C and f∈R(U). Restrict M along φ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] by applying exact restriction termwise to Q.objPreimage M. Then f satisfies the complete-element test [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-complete-element] for this restricted object if and only if φ_U(f) satisfies the same test for M over B. There are no ideal, flatness or finite-generation hypotheses.

proof.text: Module sheaves on a small slice are Grothendieck abelian, so the required unbounded derived products and multiplication-tower limits exist. On the slice C/U, apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion] to replace localization-Hom vanishing by vanishing of the derived multiplication tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. The sequential localization constructions agree by evaluating their unit endomorphisms on 1; exact restriction of chosen representatives computes the derived restriction.

proof.text: Exact scalar restriction leaves underlying complexes and multiplication maps unchanged. It preserves derived products: derived extension of scalars is its left adjoint, obtained by taking K-flat resolutions in the tensor/restriction Hom correspondence. Therefore it carries the Roos triangle of the B multiplication tower to the Roos triangle of the R tower. This identifies their derived-limit objects after restriction.

proof.text: Restriction reflects zero derived objects, since its exact underlying functor leaves cohomology abelian sheaves unchanged and reflects zero sheaves. Apply this to the isomorphic derived-limit objects and reverse the two localization-Hom criteria.

theorem restrictScalars_completeElement_iff
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : R ⟶ B)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B))]
    [hR : ∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (J.over U) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (R.over U)))]
    [hB : ∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (J.over U) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (B.over U)))]
    (M : ringedSiteDerived B) (U : C) (f : R.obj.obj (op U)) :
    letI : ∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R).over U)) := hR
    letI : ∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B).over U)) := hB
    IsRingedSiteCompleteElement J R
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage M))) U f ↔
      IsRingedSiteCompleteElement J B M U (φ.hom.app (op U) f)
